text:
sara: reproducible problem with the Python sample app async streaming and static type checkers.

sara: minimal example (from docs):

```py
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    client = AsyncClient()
    stream = client.chat.stream("gpt-slim", prompt="hi")

    async for chunk in stream:
        print(chunk.text)
```

sara: runtime works but mypy/pyright both complain: 'Object is not async iterable' / 'Iterator[ChatChunk] is not an async iterator'.

jamie: that's a bad sign. Which SDK wheel version?

sara: 0.9.3 from pip, and the docs template is the async example.

alex: can you dump the stub signature you have in site-packages?

sara: the stub shows: `def stream(self, model: str, **kwargs) -> Iterator[ChatChunk]: ...` even in the AsyncClient stubs.

mikhail: confirmed locally. Our autogen pipeline emitted `Iterator` for streaming endpoints across both clients. It's a leftover from the sync generator path.

luis: that explains multiple upstream reports. Pyright flags this strongly because it inspects declared return types.

jamie: short-term fixes: 1) instruct docs to include a small cast workaround: `from typing import cast, AsyncIterator
stream = cast(AsyncIterator[ChatChunk], client.chat.stream(...))` or 2) use `# type: ignore` on the loop. Neither is great UX.

sara: cast works for me. But we should ship correct stubs so new users don't hit this during onboarding.

mikhail: plan: update stubs generator so streaming endpoints return `AsyncIterator[...]` in async-client stubs and `Iterator[...]` in sync-client stubs. Also add a unit test that runs mypy/pyright against our sample app templates in CI.

alex: I'll open a PR with a targeted change in codegen: detect `streaming: true` + client_mode == "async" -> import AsyncIterator and emit that return type. Also add an exported alias `AsyncStream[T] = AsyncIterator[T]` in `redwood.typing` so docs can reference it consistently.

luis: exporting AsyncStream is a nice DX touch, less typing noise for users. Add it to the top-level package exports so `from redwood import AsyncStream` works.

jamie: docs/quickstarts also need a patch: remove any samples that assume sync-stub types, and add a brief troubleshooting blurb. We'll cherry-pick into a patch release if possible.

devx-bot: Created internal ticket RDW-6123 and linked draft PR (github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8021).

alex: one more nuance: some streaming chunks are typed as `Union[ChatChunk, str]` in autogen when we include raw text fallback. We should normalize to `ChatChunk | str` syntax in stubs and ensure `from __future__ import annotations` in the stubs file to keep compatibility.

mikhail: good catch. Add normalization and a small integration test that imports the generated stubs and performs `reveal_type` checks under mypy.

sara: thanks — this will remove a lot of onboarding friction. For immediate note in the docs I'm adding the cast snippet with a short explanation and a link to RDW-6123.

luis: follow-up item: check other language SDKs for parity; maybe our generator logic is shared and could cause similar issues elsewhere.

jamie: assigning follow-ups: alex -> PR for stub generator + alias export, mikhail -> CI mypy/pyright test, docs -> patch and patch release note.

sara: leaving the thread here in case others hit it. :thumbsup:

alex: I'll post updates in this thread when PR lands and when the patch wheel is cut.

mikhail: ETA for patch cut: this week if no blockers.

sara: awesome, thanks everyone.
